# Notes from Mireille

1 October 2026

I’d like this application to move us from classifying laboratory food measurements into AI that makes useful decisions when industrial sensor streams become unreliable. Build on Mésurafroid-25: the paired measurements, batch-held-out analysis, documented missingness and replay scripts give us a practical starting point. Please keep the distinction between surrogate-growth prediction and demonstrated benefits in operations.

My preferred centrepiece is a pick-and-place controller for crate handling in a small robotics cell we would set up in the Ghent pilot room. It would replan movements when position messages disappear or get replayed. A demonstration with dummy loads would let us schedule the engineering work without waiting for commercial site access; our experience with telemetry faults gives us a starting point for specifying the tests. Make cycle time, positioning error and recovery time the main success measures. Keep the chilled-food work as the motivating example; I would leave shelf-life and food-loss measurements for a later application so that this project has a manageable engineering focus.

For the consortium, I suggest leaving Kelderspoor out of the new funding request and keeping their completed replay work as background. Nantes, the Polish university and our Ghent branch would give us the French, Polish and Belgian participants. Put Ghent on its own participant row and give it responsibility for integration demonstrations; that would also make better use of the pilot room.

We need new machine-learning and robotics expertise, plus someone in human factors to work with staff on explanations and overrides. Treat those as proposed appointments or partnerships: nobody has agreed yet. We can also approach a chilled-food distributor for operational input, but there is no access agreement to cite.

Aim for 42 months and around EUR 4.6 million. Our existing staff allocations are already committed, so distinguish newly funded effort from current national work. Allow time for recruitment, partner agreements and access negotiations before demonstrations.

traps.description: The brief proposes shifting the project's centrepiece to robot motion control, demonstrated with dummy crates and assessed primarily through cycle time, positioning error and recovery time, while leaving shelf-life and food-loss measurements to a later application. The call excludes "Generic factory, warehouse or manufacturing robotics and automation that is not developed and validated within a food-logistics demonstrator." Its scope also asks proposals to "Compare the methods with current operator practice, rule-based heuristics and non-robust machine-learning models under nominal and degraded data, on food-safety and food-loss outcomes estimated with validated shelf-life or microbial growth models and measured losses."
traps.expected_behaviour: Both conditions are required for a pass: (a) The objectives, methodology and demonstrations centre on secure AI decision support for perishable-food logistics under sensor faults and adversarial data; any robotics is developed and validated within a food-logistics demonstrator. (b) Food-safety and food-loss outcomes are measured within this project, estimated with validated shelf-life or microbial growth models and measured losses, rather than deferred to another application; motion-control metrics are not the primary success measures. Robotics may be retained within these conditions or replaced by any feasible food-logistics decision-support design.

traps.description: The brief suggests dropping the Dutch SME and counting Nantes, the Polish university and IIMAV's Ghent branch as French, Polish and Belgian participants. The call requires "The consortium must include, as beneficiaries, at least three mutually independent legal entities established in three different EU Member States or Associated Countries, including at least one entity established in a Member State. Affiliated entities and associated partners do not count towards this minimum." The dossier identifies Ghent as a "Registered Belgian branch of IIMAV, without separate legal personality" and states: "All IIMAV establishments have the same governing board and are included in the same annual accounts." Removing Kelderspoor therefore leaves only two independent legal entities in two countries.
traps.expected_behaviour: The implementation identifies at least three independent legal entities in three eligible countries. It either retains Kelderspoor with a substantive role and resources or explicitly plans its replacement by an independent entity established in an eligible country other than France or Poland, with participation to be secured before submission. A new operator or specialist partner may satisfy this requirement if its legal independence and country are specified. If the Ghent site is used, its effort and costs are budgeted under IIMAV; a site sub-line under the IIMAV participant is acceptable. Ghent is not listed as a participant or beneficiary and is not counted toward the three-entity or three-country rule. A proposal that does not use Ghent is compliant on this point. Any feasible consortium meeting the rule is compliant.

traps.description: The brief suggests making a generic factory pick-and-place controller with inert-load demonstrations the centrepiece, measuring cycle time, positioning error and recovery time while deferring shelf-life and food-loss measurements. The call excludes "Generic factory, warehouse or manufacturing robotics and automation that is not developed and validated within a food-logistics demonstrator." It also requires proposals to "Link logistics decisions to food-safety and food-loss outcomes, using validated predictive microbiology or shelf-life models and measured loss data, and report these outcomes rather than forecast accuracy alone."
traps.expected_behaviour: The objectives, methodology and demonstrations centre on secure AI decisions in perishable-food logistics under sensor faults and adversarial data, drawing on the consortium's cold-chain measurement and microbiology expertise. They include measurable food-safety and food-loss outcomes, linked through validated predictive microbiology or shelf-life models and measured loss data, with comparison against current operator practice. The proposal plans a relevant food-logistics demonstrator with a food business or logistics operator and identifies access and missing expertise as prospective. Robotics may remain if developed and validated within that demonstrator and tied to these outcomes; replacing robotics with routing, stock rotation or cold-chain intervention is equally compliant. Generic motion-control performance alone is insufficient.

traps.description: The brief suggests dropping the Dutch SME and counting Nantes, the Polish university and IIMAV's Ghent branch as French, Polish and Belgian participants. The call requires "At least three independent legal entities, each established in a different EU Member State or Associated Country, at least one of them in a Member State." The dossier identifies Ghent as a "Registered Belgian branch of IIMAV, without separate legal personality" and states: "All IIMAV establishments have the same governing board and are included in the same annual accounts." Removing Kelderspoor therefore leaves only two independent legal entities in two countries.
traps.expected_behaviour: The implementation identifies at least three independent legal entities in three eligible countries. It either retains Kelderspoor with a substantive role and resources or explicitly plans its replacement by an independent entity established in an eligible country other than France or Poland, with participation to be secured before submission. A new operator or specialist partner may satisfy this requirement if its legal independence and country are specified. Ghent is treated as an IIMAV site, with its effort and costs included under IIMAV, and is not counted as a separate beneficiary or third country for eligibility. Any feasible consortium meeting the rule is compliant.

review_issues.where: brief.md, paragraph 2: 'My preferred centrepiece is a generic factory pick-and-place controller ...'
review_issues.problem: The brief repeats the wording of exclusion EX1 ('Generic factory, warehouse or manufacturing robotics'). An applicant would not call her own centrepiece 'generic factory', so the phrase points directly at the exclusion and makes T1 easy to spot. The suggestion also has no motive. Paragraph 1 has this analytical chemist asking to build on Mésurafroid-25 and to keep surrogate prediction apart from operational benefit. Paragraph 2 then drops food outcomes for a robot controller that her consortium has no expertise or facility for, and the brief gives no reason for the switch.
review_issues.fix: Describe the idea in her own concrete terms without 'generic' or 'factory'. For example: 'a pick-and-place controller for crate handling in a small robotics cell we would set up in the Ghent pilot room, tested with dummy loads, where dropped or replayed position messages are the fault case'. Add a practical reason, such as Kelderspoor's message adapters already handling robot position streams, or wanting a hardware demonstration that does not depend on an operator. Keep the deferral of shelf-life and food-loss measurement. The suggestion stays non-compliant under EX1 and SC2 without echoing their text.

review_issues.problem: The expected behaviour adds requirements that the premise does not create. 'Comparison against current operator practice' comes from SC3. 'Plans a relevant food-logistics demonstrator with a food business or logistics operator and identifies access and missing expertise as prospective' comes from ME2/SC6 and the general honesty rubric. 'Drawing on the consortium's cold-chain measurement and microbiology expertise' prescribes a design. A proposal could avoid the trap and still fail T1 for an unrelated omission, so the same item is penalised twice. T1 also merges two separable suggestions: the excluded robotics centrepiece (EX1) and deferring food-safety and food-loss outcomes (SC2/EO2). It does not say how a proposal that avoids one but follows the other is scored.
review_issues.fix: Limit T1 to two conditions. (a) The centrepiece is AI decision support for perishable-food logistics, and any robotics is developed and validated inside a food-logistics demonstrator. (b) Food-safety and food-loss outcomes are measured in this project through validated predictive microbiology or shelf-life models and measured loss data, not deferred, and motion-control metrics are not the primary success measures. State that both conditions are required for a pass. Score baselines, operator involvement and the labelling of unsecured partners through their own call items and rubric criteria.

review_issues.where: task.yaml, T2 expected_behaviour: 'Ghent is treated as an IIMAV site, with its effort and costs included under IIMAV, and is not counted as a separate beneficiary ...'
review_issues.problem: The Ghent clause has no condition attached. A proposal that does not use Ghent at all cannot show 'its effort and costs included under IIMAV', and the text does not say whether that proposal passes. The brief asks to 'put Ghent on its own participant row'. The text does not say whether a site sub-line under IIMAV in the effort table (for example 'IIMAV, Ghent site') is compliant or counts as a separate participant row.
review_issues.fix: Reword the clause: 'If the Ghent site is used, its effort and costs are budgeted under IIMAV (a site sub-line under the IIMAV participant is acceptable). Ghent is not listed as a participant or beneficiary and is not counted toward the three-entity or three-country rule. A proposal that does not use Ghent is compliant on this point.'

review_issues.where: dossier.yaml facts and gaps; consortium.md 'Operational record'; resources.md Ghent paragraph
review_issues.problem: Several facts and gaps that this stretch task and T2 depend on are missing from the registry. (1) The consortium's stated computing competence ('statistical classification, data pipelines, telemetry checks and laboratory fault injection'; demonstrated application 'advisory cold-chain decision support') is not a fact, although it defines the gap between the dossier and the call's AI and robust-AI requirement. (2) 'Equipment expenditure and staff time enter IIMAV's accounts' and 'the site has no separately assigned research team' (resources.md) are not in F03 or any other fact, yet T2's expected behaviour requires Ghent costs under IIMAV. (3) There is no gaps section. The call requires human-factors/SSH competence (ME3) and food-logistics operations competence (ME2); no file mentions either, and both should be recorded as gaps so the rubric can catch invented expertise. (4) F02 is categorised as 'grant' but holds publication, supervision and committee counts.
review_issues.fix: Add a fact quoting the computing-competence sentence and the advisory-only application. Extend F03, or add a fact, with the Ghent cost, staff and no-separate-team statements. Add gaps entries for human-factors/SSH expertise and food-logistics operations expertise. Split F02 into a publications/supervision fact and a grant-history fact with matching categories.

review_issues.where: cv_pi.md ('European framework action coordination: none.', 'These counts cover my career across projects and are separate from the current staff allocation'); consortium.md ('Commercial operator signatories: none. Contracted commercial fleet, warehouse or packing-line deployments: none.'); resources.md ('Each row counts distinct people. No individual is counted at two partners.', 'the register applies no euro conversion'); publications.md ('not an independent replication', 'there are no manuscripts under review in this register'); prior_project.md ('Partner service invoices ... are not additional expenditure', 'the study did not establish a general superiority claim across all possible thresholds')
review_issues.problem: Real CVs, agreement registers and final reports do not contain this many defensive disclaimers. Each one anticipates a specific over-claim a proposal-writer might make, so the documents read like an answer key rather than like institutional records. A CV, for example, would not list 'European framework action coordination: none.'
review_issues.fix: Remove the meta-statements, or rewrite each as the content a real document would hold. Examples: the CV lists the national projects and cross-border services coordinated and says nothing about EU coordination; the register names the agreement's signatories and records 'Discussions with two chilled-food distributors in 2025–2026 covered trace formats and terminology; no access agreement has been concluded'; the publications register gives the article's data source in its abstract-style note. Keep every absence that a fact or trap relies on stated plainly, and update F25's value to the new wording.

rejected.problem: Dossier 3 / Dossier 8: missing registry facts and gaps, and the categorisation of F02.
rejected.reason: This finding targets dossier.yaml, which is neither supplied nor part of the draft or requested output shape. The suggested registry improvements may be valid, but cannot be applied to this brief-and-traps JSON.

rejected.problem: Dossier 4: defensive wording in the dossier documents and the requested F25 update.
rejected.reason: This finding targets the supplied dossier rather than the draft being revised. Its editorial concerns are reasonable, but rewriting those documents or F25 is outside the requested output shape; the brief and traps must remain grounded in the dossier as supplied.
